title: Tokenization
interviewAnswer: Tokenization converts text into a sequence of discrete token IDs. Subword methods balance vocabulary size and sequence length and must match the model’s training tokenizer exactly.
why: Tokenization defines the units language models operate on and directly affects context length, multilingual/code behavior and cost.
intuition: A tokenizer converts raw text into integer token IDs from a finite vocabulary. Modern subword tokenizers balance whole-word efficiency with the ability to represent unseen words.
deepDive: BPE/WordPiece/Unigram learn subword vocabularies from corpora. The same visible string can tokenize differently across models. Token count—not character/word count—drives context usage and inference cost. Special tokens encode boundaries/control signals. Byte-level schemes guarantee coverage but may use more tokens for some languages/domains.
workedExample: A rare technical identifier may split into many subword tokens, consuming context and potentially weakening semantic representation compared with common words.
commonMistakes: Assuming one token equals one word.
Using a tokenizer from a different model than the embedding/LLM weights.
Hard-coding character limits when the real constraint is tokens.
followUps: How does token count affect cost?
production: Estimate/request limits in tokens, version tokenizer with the model, and handle truncation/chunking explicitly.
